title: feat(cl): translate, XY turn, A/B turn and vertical mirror for toolpaths
body:
## What changed

- A new module `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` with three sub-files (`transform_rotary.rs`, `transform_mirror.rs`, `transform_climb.rs`). `camcraft-app` re-exports it as `app::cl::transform`.
- `translate(tp, [dx, dy, dz])` shifts every move, arc center, canned cycle, compensated span and edge break.
- `transform_xy(tp, tx, ty, angle_deg, pivot)` turns the path in XY about a pivot and then shifts it. Nesting (#2166) can call it directly.
- `rotate_about_axis(tp, RotaryAxis::A | B, origin, angle_deg, chord_tol)` turns the path about X or Y. Each move states the turned tool axis. Arcs become chords within `chord_tol`, or return `ArcChordTolerance`.
- `mirror_plane(tp, MirrorPlane, MirrorMode)` mirrors the path across a vertical plane.
  - `GeometricMirror` gives the exact mirror image: G2 <-> G3 and G41 <-> G42.
  - `PreserveClimb(PassFamily)` mirrors and then runs each pass backwards between its entry and its retract. The lead-out becomes the lead-in. The arcs keep their original G2/G3, and the compensated spans keep their original side.
- `TransformError` names each refusal: `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, `RotaryMove`, `TiltedMove`, `PlasmaCut`, `VerticalArc`, `CannedCycleTilt`, `FineBoreShift`, `ArcChordTolerance`, `HorizontalMirrorPlane`, `TiltedMirrorPlane`, `BadInput`, `NotReversible(why)`.
- The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3011-cl-transforms.md`.

## Cause

This is new work. The codebase had no shared transform for toolpaths. Patterns, mirror folders and nesting need one.

## Design

- All four transforms use one map, `p -> M p + t`, with `M` orthogonal.
- An arc keeps its plane only when `M` maps the plane normal exactly onto plus or minus itself. Its turn direction flips when `det(M)` times that sign is negative. This one rule gives the G2/G3 swap under a mirror. It also finds the XZ / YZ arcs that a transform cannot keep.
- Moves, arc centers and cycles snap to the coordinate lattice. Edge-break polylines do not snap, because a snap would move framed caps off orthonormal.
- `PreserveClimb` accepts only contour, profile and chamfer paths. It refuses these by name:
  - a helical ramp, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing and other families;
  - a ramp or helical entry;
  - a level change without a retract;
  - a cut before the first pass or after the last pass;
  - a link that is not on the clearance plane.

## Latest review fix (second safety read on `91cd4fe1a`)

1. **Fine boring under a turn or a mirror.** A `CycleKind::FineBore` cycle shifts the tip with a lateral rapid at the hole bottom. The oriented spindle stop fixes that direction on the machine. `transform_xy` and `mirror_plane` now refuse a fine-bore cycle when the matrix is not the identity, with the new error `FineBoreShift`. `translate` and a whole turn (0 or 360 degrees) still accept it. `rotate_about_axis` refuses every cycle already.
2. **`PreserveClimb` leads.** The reversed pass plunges where the old pass left its cut. The cl layer cannot tell a lead from the contour. The reversal now requires symmetry: the first cut move and the last cut move have one shape (straight or arc) and one length, within 2 um. A pass with a lead-in and no lead-out, or with a shorter lead-out, is refused by name with `NotReversible`.
3. **Notes.** The decision file now says that a geometric mirror of a thread-milling helix changes the hand of the thread. It also says that heights outside the path do not move with a Z translate.

New pins:

- `fine_bore_refuses_an_xy_turn_and_a_mirror_and_translates` (`transform_tests.rs`): a 180 and a 90 degree turn and a mirror refuse; a translate and a 360 degree turn accept; a drill cycle still turns and mirrors.
- `preserve_climb_refuses_a_lead_in_without_a_lead_out` (`transform_mirror_tests.rs`): the review case (5 mm lead-in, no lead-out) and a 2 mm lead-out refuse; a matching 5 mm lead-out reverses, and the reversed plunge is in the air.

Pin proof: I disabled the two new checks (`if false && ...`). `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform` was RED: 24 passed, 2 failed (the two new pins). I restored the checks: GREEN, 26 passed.

Head: `b0efe2ee629a83ac78f732bdb3dbc639025ad824`. Base: `upstream/main` at `44c13a01d8879fbdcd424ca6653e61b5ecd9d12b`.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`: GREEN, 26 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,077 steps, 0 failed, 16.2 minutes. It includes `cl suites: lib`, `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl` and `clippy -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 241 steps, 0 failed, 28.3 minutes.

Goldens moved: none. The catalog and `golden_cl` suites ran and passed. No recorded program changed.

Not exercised: a trial merge with `upstream/main`. The runs test the PR head. A helix arc and an edge-break cap under a turn or a mirror still have no pin.

## Earlier review fix (collapsed arcs)

The latest review found that a collapsed arc could remove a tool axis change. Rounded chord endpoints could match after a preceding move at another pose.

The rotary transform now drops a collapsed chord only when its axis also matches the last emitted pose. It retains a changed axis as a straight move at the standing tip. The move keeps its kind and feed. The same rule retains an initial collapsed arc that states a pose. A distance tolerance cannot permit removal of a required rotation.

## Tests (pins)

The original 20 tests are in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_tests.rs` and `transform_mirror_tests.rs` (`cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`):

- `translate_shifts_every_record_to_the_micron`, `translate_refuses_a_non_finite_offset`
- `transform_xy_turns_a_quarter_about_the_pivot_then_shifts`, `transform_xy_at_thirty_degrees_is_micron_accurate`, `transform_xy_refuses_a_vertical_arc_it_cannot_keep`
- `rotate_about_a_turns_the_point_and_states_the_axis`, `rotate_about_b_flattens_arcs_within_the_chord_tolerance`, `rotate_about_an_axis_by_zero_is_the_identity`, `rotate_about_an_axis_refuses_a_tilted_canned_cycle`
- `every_transform_refuses_thread_cycles_probe_touches_and_c_moves`
- `geometric_mirror_swaps_g2_g3_and_g41_g42`, `geometric_mirror_on_a_diagonal_plane_is_micron_accurate`, `mirror_refuses_horizontal_and_tilted_planes`, `mirror_refuses_tilted_moves`
- `preserve_climb_reverses_the_pass_between_entry_and_retract`, `preserve_climb_reverses_two_depths_linked_on_the_clearance_plane`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_helical_entry`, `preserve_climb_refuses_clearing_families_by_name`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_cut_before_the_first_pass`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_level_change_without_a_retract`

The initial implementation report states that these pins did not compile before the API existed.

This round adds `rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses`. It checks a short arc after a rapid at another pose. It checks the transformed axis, standing tip, feed, move kind and chain. It also checks the straight-feed control and the unchanged-pose control.

Final head: `91cd4fe1a54a2aae98b95241bbcbbdf563f54c05`.

Pin proof for this round: the verifier saved the fixed rotary source outside the repository. It replaced only that source with the reviewed version from `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`. The new pin stayed in place.

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses -- --nocapture
```

Result: RED, 0 passed and 1 failed. The test expected two moves but received one. The verifier restored the fix and ran:

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform
```

Result: GREEN, all 24 transform tests passed.

## Previous review fix and evidence

The previous review found that the arc sampler stops at 1,024 chords. A 1,000 mm semicircle exceeded the requested 0.0001 mm tolerance.

The rotary transform retains that bounded sampler. It samples at half the requested tolerance. It checks the curve error for the actual chord count and adds the endpoint rounding error. Circular arcs use the sagitta bound. Radius ramps use the sampler's second derivative bound. `ArcChordTolerance` refuses a path when the total bound exceeds `chord_tol`.

That round added these three pins:

- `rotate_about_a_refuses_an_arc_beyond_the_chord_budget`: refuses the review case. It also measures chord midpoint error on an accepted 1,000 mm semicircle.
- `rotate_about_b_bounds_arc_midpoints_in_each_plane`: measures analytic curve midpoint error in XY, XZ and YZ. It covers circular arcs, radius ramps, normal interpolation and both turn directions.
- `rotate_about_a_refuses_rounding_beyond_the_chord_tolerance`: refuses an arc whose endpoint rounding exceeds the tolerance.

Historical proof on `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`: restoring the rotary source from `a273ee018` made two pins fail. The chord-budget and rounding-refusal pins failed. Restoring the fix made all 23 transform tests pass. These results describe the previous round.

The initial implementation report records these mutation results:

- the G2/G3 flip: 3 pins red
- the G41/G42 swap: 2 pins red
- the side restore in the climb reversal: 1 pin red
- the probe refusal: 1 pin red
- the refusal of a cut before the first pass: 1 pin red
- the horizontal-plane refusal: 1 pin red
- the pass reversal: 2 pins red
- the tilted-cycle refusal: 1 pin red

## Earlier validation (head 91cd4fe1a)

Validation head: `91cd4fe1a54a2aae98b95241bbcbbdf563f54c05`.

Quick base: `60376ccbbfa52305db6fa880278222e7854fcdbf` (`upstream/main` at quick start).

Heavy base: `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344` (`upstream/main` at heavy start). Another session advanced the shared ref before heavy started.

Both bases have merge base `d911f45535df24c42d5fde5feaed386c5fca4907` with this head. The selected eight-file diff is unchanged. The commands test the PR head directly. No trial merge was tested.

- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`: GREEN, 24 passed after restoration.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,077 steps, 0 failed, 20.9 minutes.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN, 0.87 seconds. The quick gate also passed clippy for all selected crates, with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`, in 37 seconds.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 241 steps, 0 failed, 42.9 minutes. Registered known-fail checks matched their expected results.
- `app suites: example_catalog`: GREEN, 34 passed and 4 ignored.
- `app heavy: example_catalog`: GREEN, the remaining 4 passed. All 38 catalog cases passed across the debug and heavy steps.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive` and `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: GREEN, 1 passed each.
- `app suites: golden_cl`: GREEN, 33 passed.
- `git diff --check`: GREEN. The tracked worktree is clean at the final head.

UI screenshots: not applicable. This PR changes no UI code or assets.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog and reached golden suites ran. No recorded program changed or required regeneration.

## Not exercised

- No caller exists yet: patterns, mirror folders and nesting (#2166) will use it.
- No posted G-code goes through a transformed path in this PR.
- The framed edge-break caps under a turn and under a mirror are not pinned by a test.
- Integration with the current `upstream/main` was not tested. These runs test the PR head directly.

## Overlaps

#3046 adds a line to the module list of `crates/cl/src/cl/mod.rs`. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: CL toolpath transforms: translate, XY turn, A/B axis turn and vertical-plane mirror (G2/G3 and G41/G42 swap, or a climb-preserving pass reversal), with named refusals.

Fixes #3011
